fit.title: Operating cash-flow DCF
fit.reason: Value forecast operating cash flows and reinvestment, then cross-check with comparable P/E or EV/EBITDA. A dividend-only model can miss cash returned through buybacks or retained for growth.
fit.caution: Review business mix, cash-flow quality, dilution, margins and reinvestment before relying on forecasts.
fit.statement: No model is always most accurate. This is an explainable starting point, not a verified survey of current Wall Street analyst usage.

These historical facts were source-reviewed on 2026-10-17. They are a dated supplement, not an automatically synchronized issuer feed. A new release, restatement or corporate action requires a new review.

These are historical reported financial facts through June 30, 2026; no current stock quote, market capitalization, fully diluted October share count, earnings forecast or intrinsic-value conclusion is added.

Each TTM monetary flow uses FY2025 + H1 2026 − H1 2025 from two official statement sources. No quarterly/YTD EPS or weighted-average share count is added, subtracted or annualized to manufacture an annual EPS or TTM denominator.

The latest H1 diluted-share average is 609.7m and the period-end common count is 604.9m. The separate reviewed DCF uses a 605.9m proxy (604.9m plus Q2 incremental dilution 1.0m); this supplement does not change that reviewed forecast, bridge or value.

Capex is gross reported property additions C$1,134m in H1 2026, C$1,324m in H1 2025 and C$3,658m in FY2025. Asset-sale proceeds, other investing cash flows, issuer non-GAAP free cash flow and management net-capex guidance are not substituted for gross capex or labeled FCFF.

Cash excludes restricted cash C$14m; debt includes commercial paper and finance leases but excludes operating lease liabilities and pension obligations. The reviewed DCF separately handles pensions and leases.

Payables includes accounts payable and other, so the normalized point-in-time receivables + supplies − payables arithmetic is not a complete operating working-capital roll-forward. The reviewed DCF retains its separately reviewed cash-flow-row working-capital treatment.
A separate diluted-common-income numerator is not asserted for all three periods; exact reported net income and diluted EPS are retained without deriving an unreported numerator from rounded EPS.

Payables includes accounts payable and other, so the normalized point-in-time receivables + supplies − payables arithmetic is not a complete operating working-capital roll-forward. The reviewed DCF retains its separately reviewed cash-flow-row working-capital treatment.
A separate diluted-common-income numerator is not asserted for all three periods; exact reported net income and diluted EPS are retained without deriving an unreported numerator from rounded EPS.
